Well of course my initial reaction was a mix of fear and awe. Imagine sitting in your drab grey office plugging away at some tedious budget changes and contractor details when you look out your only window and see what looks like a giant shadow of a creature lumbering in the distance.

I don't like admit it but I thought someone was pulling my leg. I tapped at my window wondering what kind of screen or technology was used in order to manage the overlay I was seeing. The details looked so fantastical. The hundreds of feet tall creature fit in perfectly with the background and its off green skin reminded me of moss. I remember thinking that nothing that large could possible walk on those small front stalks and that whoever created the creature ought to have thought the design through a bit better. It was so convincing too. My stubborn pride was the only thing that kept me from getting up and out my office to discuss it with my nearest coworker. I wasn't going to give the prankster the satisfaction of seeing me leave my office in bewilderment in order start gossiping about the creature.

It was damn near twenty minutes that passed by before the shaking was strong enough to convince me it wasn't a joke and the shaking wasn't just in my head. The creature's path was bringing it closer and as I watched it take steps I could almost see the wave of pressure move through the Earth and eventually hit our building. That's when I realized how quiet everything was. I had stood up and taken off my headset to closer inspect my window. The sales people who normally buzzed outside my office door were silent. The only sound was a far off steady rumble.

The creatures mere existence shocked humanity and news spread across the planet in a matter of hours. That was precisely three years ago from today...

The titan looked down on the world before it, weighing up the souls it wanted to devour.

The fishing town sat before it.

Tenshar gazed upon the gazer from up on his hill. Today would be an interesting day, that was for sure.

The anomaly had opened from the moon, it was no accident, a sigil burned bright in the sky, eclipsing the stars. The largest glyph ever to be activated, and it was used in an act of terrorism. The mystics on the surface decoded it in horror and soon the entire council of elders had been summoned to address this threat.

There was a small offense onto the rogue mages on the moon, but too much magic draws demons, and that would only accelerate their plans. The sigils purpose was to open a portal to the warp, the genius in the design was that it drank any magic in the area around it, so the attacks the council made just fueled it to go faster.

This obviously did not go unnoticed by the Cerric population, the majority of people on Earth, those that did not know about magic. It did not take long before the council had to declare magic public. This caused almost as many problems as the encroaching apocalypse.

Two weeks later the sigil flared and died, and in it's place the promised portal into the warp opened up, swallowing the moon and causing a giant tear in the sky.

It didn't take long for the first demons to come through, but what was first a few curious sprites became a torrent of greater demons and worse.

The magical community were held responsible by the Cerric, and so were expected to cull the tide of monsters that came out.

This was the first titan to come through, and it had almost certainly come for him. The old Councillor cracked his knuckles and prepared himself.

He found his vault and removed from it some of the crystals he kept there, also in there was his old council staff, he sighed as he saw it, but left it be. Instead he found his usual staff, a far less ornate one at that, but with a stronger crystal at the top, and the hexes binding it he'd cast himself, so it was probably more reliable than the one he'd been awarded anyway. Probably.

He walked out into his courtyard and activated the sigils he'd buried deep in the stonework. There was a bright blue glow as they awakened from their slumber. He checked over them, reinforced them as much as he could, and set about the next step of the project that had seen him expelled from the council.

The titan was slow and lumbering, he probably had enough time to finish the incant, and if not the shielding on his sprawling house would probably hold it at bay for long enough. Probably.

The crystals that he'd sworn to destroy fit perfectly in place in the ornament in the middle of the courtyard. He then awakened the magic in the ornament itself: gravitational exclusion magic, inward facing shielding, magic compression and the emergency sigils that would turn the magic into an explosion that would rival the most powerful Cerric hydrogen bomb if anything went wrong. The thought of that being the failsafe made him shudder, it was small wonder that this had been reason to have him expelled from the council.

He stood in position, built up the shielding magic around him more than he thought would be necessary, then started his incant.

It was a magical summoning, from the warp, in a similar style to the sigil the rogue mages used, but this time it was the raw power the warp contained that he was using. The crystals in the middle hummed in resonance with each other as the power gathered between them, glowing brighter and brighter until Tenshar had to hastily throw up a sigil to block the light. The words flowed from his mouth in a perfect stream, the magic he'd devoted years to make, tweaking it, making it perfect. Most magic could have it's creases ironed out in practice, but he had to do everything in theory.

The instability of the magic had begun to show, the magic leaked from the inner shielding, lessor demons in the area caught the scent and began hammering at the outer wards of the old Councillor's property. The titan now stared at nothing but the house, it's gaze no longer sweeping but instead transfixed on the blazing light up the hill.

More and more magic gathered, bolts of energy blasted out of the shielding, tearing apart the courtyard and house. The shields Tenshar had around himself quivered as these bolts hit, but thankfully held. The summoning continued and now the stonework at the base of the ornament had started melting, he quickly added levitation sigils to keep the crystals in place before the solid mithril ornament sank into the ground.

All the demons for mile had now caught scent, and an army of them were battling against his wards, they may pose a threat before the titan even got there, but Tenshar trusted his magics and carried on regardless.

In the center of the ornament a ball of pure magical energy was forming, bound by layers and layers of seals the magic it contained was still leaking out at horrifying rates. An eldrict storm had formed overhead, a strange mage-mist enveloping the property, corrupting the unfortunate plants and animals caught within.

Now came the most dangerous part, there was enough energy there, he just had to make it stable. He used the magical compression sigils to try and shrink the ball of energy. It hit the ball in hammer blows of force, each time magnitudes more energy leaked the seals, testing the integrity of Tenshar's own shields, ripping apart his own wards from the inside and obliterating what was left of the house. What wasn't magma was rubble, nothing but the small circle of stone he stood on himself was still intact.

Eventually the pulses stopped, the storm began to fade, the bolts of energy ceased and Tenshar stood there cackling. He drew the orb towards him, added a few extra sigils to help maintain it and held it before him. A kugelbliz, it was the size of a marble, an iota of energy so dense that it's own gravity keeps it stable, with gravity exclusion magic keeping it from consuming the entire planet under it's relentless gravitational hunger.

The wards of his property finally failed, the titan was upon him and he began writing a single glyph in the air as the shields around him buckled under the might of the titan.

He then activated the glyph written before him in tears in the fabric of reality. It was easily the most powerful magic that had ever been invoked, yet the glyph read only two words: Terra ablution.

Addiction to drugs is usually framed as a distinct phenomenon from the usual urges we have to eat, breath, have sex, and so on. As a thoughtful human being and a person who's been addicted to some drugs and isn't any more, I find this puzzling.

Consider this: every day, I feel compelled to eat. If I don't eat, I feel pretty lousy. When I eat, I love it - it's so good. Yum!

I could get really into eating, and eat tons of tasty snacks all the time. If I did, I'd get really fat after awhile. I'm not overweight, by the way - but I can easily see why. I don't eat junk food, and exercise all the time. But when I have snacks in my house, I totally eat them (e.g. if someone gives me cookies as a gift, they're gone in a day). I don't feel good about it, so I don't buy snack food, and I don't get out of hand with eating.

If I did though, and got huge and just kept buying cookies and eating them, you'd probably say I had a food addiction (I sure would). It seems to me, subjectively, to be about the same as my former addictions to drugs; if I kept a carton of cigarettes in my house, you bet I'd start smoking again eventually. And then I'd feel like shit, and keep smoking cause I'd have built up that need again, and we'd all say I was addicted.

But when I quit smoking, I stopped getting cravings. I could incite them if I tried (e.g. by buying a carton and leaving it on my desk for weeks). But they don't come unless the situation provokes it quite strongly.

Food, though - I crave that shit every ~5 hours, without fail. Doesn't that seem like an addiction to you?

It does to me.

What do you think?
Is drug addiction really that different from other compulsive activities, such as eating and sex?

Think of it as that "nudge in the wrong direction" way of thought.

Smoking is physiologically and mentally addictive, and you also form environmental and social habits around it. It's not a lot of fun when you feel absolutely on edge because of low nicotine, and you start shaking and sweating until you get a cigarette.

Some people with severe addictions cannot cope without even having anything on hand, and their brain will only function towards the knowledge that they can escape soon or later on. It sounds like you got lucky and didn't develop a strong addiction to it (addiction rates seem to be hereditary, ie alcoholism in families).

Eating different types of food can be addictive, like you said about sugary foods. Your body wants it because it is easy energy, but if you don't do anything you get fat. But since you need to eat a specific amount of and variety of food to stay healthy I wouldn't call eating an addiction, but a necessity.

You can always over imbibe in anything, but the continued, habitual use with the knowledge that it is harmful will put it in a classification of addiction.

I think in some ways that makes sense and in some ways it's not a fair comparison.

First of all, part of the definition of an addiction is that it in some way disrupts your life. Even if you eat a cookie everyday, it isn't going to fuck up your life, it isn't going to fuck up your relationships. You're not gonna rob someone so that you can buy one more cookie.

Also, although you can become psychologically dependent on pretty much anything, there is a difference between that and chemically based addictions. You could make the argument that the sugar and fat content in some food invokes similar chemical responses in the body, but I've never heard of anyone going into fat or sugar withdrawal (Excepting maybe diabetics).

I also think it is unfair to think of anything that you actually need to survive as an addiction. Eating is healthy. Breathing is healthy. Drinking a pint of vodka a night is not healthy. Maybe that's the important distinction?

Also, although you can become psychologically dependent on pretty much anything, there is a difference between that and chemically based addictions. You could make the argument that the sugar and fat content in some food invokes similar chemical responses in the body, but I've never heard of anyone going into fat or sugar withdrawal (Excepting maybe diabetics).

Here, though, you're conflating withdrawal and addiction. In fact, the same reward circuit in the brain is responsible for both drug cravings / reward and food cravings / reward - they are both chemically based addictions. When you have sex, or eat delicious food, or rail a line of coke, your reward center in the nucleus accumbens says "THAT WAS A GREAT IDEA, DO IT AGAIN SOME TIME". In some people and life situations, that leads to a habit that's quite hard to break.

It seems to me the only potential means of differentiating the two you've offered is on the basis of harm or health. I don't find that convincing at all, though; it seems to me that uncontrollable craving is a far better defining characteristic of addiction (outside of mental health treatment manuals, where a practical disease model definition is necessary). I mean, I could get addicted to a drug that's good for me too; many people who suffer from anxiety get addicted to benzodiazepines prescribed by their doctors, for example.

We've got the same brain circuits running to produce the same sort of subjective experience ("that was great, let's do it again soon") and pattern of behavior (consistent, sustained repetition). Why not call it addiction?

I think it shouldn't be called addiction because that carries a lot of baggage. If you refer to our dependence on food as addiction it takes weight away from the word and people with serious problems may not feel that it accurately describes them anymore.

I think risk to health is the most important defining feature of addiction. I guess it's true that you can be addicted and have cravings without having a risk to your health, but then who cares? The only point in labeling addiction is to treat it, and if there is no risk to health or lifestyle there is no need for treatment.

Providing an Initial Public Offering (IPO) does not provide the creators cash on hand. Cash is very liquid, stock not as liquid and the price of stock fluctuates more than the price of cash. When a company IPO's, typically executives are not allowed to sell their stock for some time and seeing that you generally cannot use stock to pay rent or employees, this can be very troublesome to a company.

When a CEO or person who is highly regarded from within a company begins to sell off their interest, this is often seen as a sign of weakness within the company and the stock price can plummet while he is trying to liquidate his assets. Hence he could have 10 billion dollars in stock, then sell all his shares (a bad idea) and only return 1 billion.

The answer to your question is "Maybe?". Main points, Stock != cash, Stock price fluctuates a lot over time, one should never invest a large amount of their capital in a single venture. Finally we do not know the financials, we do not know the future of the company, and we do not know Markus Frind. So, Maybe?
